# 03 · Base.astro, aurora, single scroll listener — spec

Issue: [PV3-8](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-8) · Branch: `feat/03-base-layout`
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-portfolio-v3-design.md` §3, §6 · `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §2 (spacing), §3 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §4

## Goal

The layout every page mounts into, and the scroll engine every later motion issue hooks
onto. After this block, adding a section means writing a component — never touching the
head, the container, or the scroll wiring.

## Context

`src/pages/index.astro` and `src/pages/en/index.astro` currently duplicate, verbatim:
the whole `<head>`, the inline theme + language script, the two font preloads, the three
`hreflang` alternates, and the language toggle anchor. Issue 02 left it that way on
purpose. All of it moves here, and the pages shrink to `lang` + content.

`src/lib/content.ts` exports `content`, `links`, `stack`, `consoleLog`, `site`.
`src/lib/i18n.ts` exports `langFromPath`, `siblingPath`, `DEFAULT_LANG`.

## Scope

### 1. `src/layouts/Base.astro`

Props: `lang: Lang`. Everything else derives from it (`t`, `otherLang`, `siblingHref`).

Owns:

- The full `<head>`: charset, viewport, favicon, `<title>` (`${site.name} · ${t.eyebrow}`),
  `<meta name="description">` (`t.heroSub`), the three `hreflang` alternates,
  `<link rel="canonical">`.
- Open Graph and Twitter card tags: `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:type`,
  `og:locale` (`es_AR` / `en_US`), `og:image` → `${links.domain}/og.png`,
  `twitter:card` = `summary_large_image`. **`public/og.png` does not exist yet** — that
  is fine, the tags ship and the file arrives with the deploy issue. Do not invent one.
- The two font preloads.
- The inline theme + language script, moved verbatim from the pages. It stays
  `is:inline` and keeps receiving `otherLang` / `siblingHref` through `define:vars`.
- `<html lang={lang}>`, `<body>`, the aurora, and slots.

Slots: a default `<slot />` for the page content, plus named `nav` and `footer` slots.
Issues 04 and 14 fill those; until then a page that provides neither renders fine.

### 2. Layout utilities

In `src/styles/app.css`, using Tailwind v4's `@utility`, so components stop repeating
the magic numbers:

- `container-page` — `max-width: 1200px; margin-inline: auto; padding-inline: clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px)`
- `section-y` — `padding-block: clamp(56px, 7vw, 100px)`
- `section-divider` — `border-top: 1px solid var(--color-line)`

Hero padding (`clamp(72px,10vw,140px)` top / `clamp(64px,8vw,110px)` bottom) is not a
utility: it appears once, in issue 05.

### 3. Aurora

Three blobs: `position: fixed`, `border-radius: 50%`, `filter: blur(90–100px)`,
`z-index: 0`, colors accent@.16–.22 and violet@.14, sitting behind `<main>`.
Animations `aur1` 16s / `aur2` 20s / `aur1` 24s, all `alternate` — the keyframes already
exist in `app.css` from issue 01.

`aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none`. On viewports under 720px, only two blobs render
(`MOTION_SPEC` §13).

The aurora is the only thing painted at `z-index: 0`; page content sits above it.

### 4. `src/lib/motion/scroll.ts` — the single listener

The **only** `scroll` listener in the site. rAF-throttled: the event sets a flag, the
frame does the work, so a burst of events collapses into one read.

```ts
export type ScrollState = { scrollY: number; vh: number; progress: number }
export function onScroll(fn: (s: ScrollState) => void): () => void
```

`onScroll` registers a subscriber and returns an unsubscribe. The listener attaches on
the first subscription and detaches when the last one leaves. Every subscriber gets the
same `ScrollState`, computed once per frame — no subscriber may call
`getBoundingClientRect` on its own during the frame if the value is already in the state.

`progress` is the document progress of `MOTION_SPEC` §4:
`scrollY / (scrollHeight - vh)`, clamped to `[0, 1]`, and `0` when the document does not
scroll (guard the division by zero).

Also listens to `resize` to refresh `vh`, throttled the same way.

Issues 08 and 09 subscribe here. They must not add a listener of their own.

### 5. `src/lib/motion/math.ts` — pure functions

Starts here and grows with each motion issue. All pure, all unit-tested without a DOM.

```ts
docProgress(scrollY: number, scrollHeight: number, vh: number): number
auroraStyle(p: number): { filter: string; opacity: number; translateY: string }
```

`auroraStyle` implements `MOTION_SPEC` §4 exactly:
`filter: hue-rotate(${p*260}deg) saturate(${1 + 0.4*p})`,
`opacity` ramping `.45 → 1` across the first 40% of the document (so `p ≥ .4` is `1`),
`translateY: ${-12 * p}vh`.

### 6. Reduced motion

A shared `src/lib/motion/reduced.ts` exporting `prefersReducedMotion(): boolean`, used
by every motion module from here on.

With `reduce`: the aurora renders static (no CSS animation, no scroll updates) and
`scroll.ts` never attaches a listener. Content is unaffected — the aurora is decoration.

### 7. Pages

`index.astro` and `en/index.astro` shrink to: import `Base`, set `lang`, render the
content block inside it. All duplicated head markup is gone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: `docProgress` returns 0 at the top, 1 at the bottom, clamps beyond both, and returns 0 when `scrollHeight === vh`.
- [ ] `bun test`: `auroraStyle(p)` matches `MOTION_SPEC` §4 at p=0, p=.2, p=.4 and p=1 — including that opacity reaches 1 at .4 and stays there.
- [ ] `bun test`: `onScroll` runs its subscribers once per frame, not once per event (fire N synthetic scroll events against one rAF tick, assert one call).
- [ ] `bun test`: unsubscribing the last subscriber removes the listener; subscribing again re-attaches it.
- [ ] `bun test`: with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `onScroll` never attaches a listener.
- [ ] `bun run build` then grep `dist/`: exactly one `addEventListener('scroll'` across all shipped JavaScript.
- [ ] Both pages use `Base.astro`, and `dist/index.html` / `dist/en/index.html` differ only by language-dependent content (same tag structure, same head shape).
- [ ] The head carries: canonical, description, the three hreflang alternates, og:title / og:description / og:url / og:type / og:locale / og:image, twitter:card.
- [ ] The aurora is `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none`, and behind the content.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled, both pages render fully and the aurora still shows.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

Nav, hero, any section component, the visible theme toggle, the reveal observer, the
node canvas. The `nav` and `footer` slots stay empty in this block.

No puedo tocar la configuración de integraciones de Linear desde acá — el MCP expone issues, proyectos y docs, no settings de workspace. Y mi token de GitHub no tiene el scope para listar instalaciones de Apps. Lo que sí pude verificar del lado de GitHub:

- `djmaam/portfolio-v3` es **privado**, y el owner es una **cuenta personal**, no una organización.
- El repo no tiene webhooks (`[]`).

La causa más probable de que no puedas conectarlo: **un GitHub App se instala una sola vez por cuenta**. Si ya instalaste el app de Linear en `djmaam` para el workspace de Kodaiverse, esa instalación está tomada, y el workspace nuevo no puede crear una segunda sobre la misma cuenta personal.

Pasos para confirmarlo y resolverlo, en orden:

1. **Andá a https://github.com/settings/installations** y buscá "Linear". Si aparece, hacé click en *Configure* y fijate en *Repository access*: si está en "Only select repositories", agregá `portfolio-v3` a la lista. Con el repo privado y fuera de la selección, Linear no lo ve aunque el app esté instalado.

2. **En el workspace nuevo**, como admin: *Settings → Features → Integrations → GitHub → Enable*. Si el flujo de OAuth te reconoce la instalación existente, listo.

3. **Si GitHub te dice que el app ya está instalado y Linear igual no engancha el workspace nuevo**, tenés tres salidas: desconectar el app del workspace viejo, mover `portfolio-v3` a una organización de GitHub (una org es una cuenta distinta, así que admite su propia instalación), o mantener los dos workspaces y aceptar que solo uno tiene la integración.

Un detalle aparte, que aplica una vez que la conexión funcione: nuestras ramas se llaman `feat/03-base-layout`, y Linear autolinkea por nombre de rama solo si seguís su formato (`marcosarrietadev/pv3-8-...`). Lo que sí va a funcionar es el **magic word**: los cuerpos de las PR que vengo escribiendo ya dicen `Closes PV3-N`, y con eso Linear linkea y mueve el issue al mergear. Si querés que además autolinkee por rama, cambio el naming de las ramas al formato de Linear en el próximo bloque — decime.

# 04 · Nav — spec

Issue: [PV3-9](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-9) · Branch: `feat/04-nav`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.1, §4 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §1 · `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-portfolio-v3-design.md` §6, §7

## Goal

The first real component. It fills the `nav` slot `Base.astro` left empty, and it brings
in the scramble effect that issue 10 reuses for company names.

## Context

`Base.astro` exposes a `nav` slot. Both pages still render a throwaway language-toggle
anchor in their content block — **it gets deleted here**; the real toggle lives in Nav.

Available: `content.ts` (`content`, `links`, `site`), `i18n.ts` (`siblingPath`),
`theme.ts` (`getTheme`, `setTheme`, `toggleTheme`), `motion/reduced.ts`,
`motion/scroll.ts`, `motion/math.ts`.

Nav copy keys in `content.json`: `navAbout`, `navWork`, `navProjects`, `navContact`.

## Scope

### 1. `src/components/Nav.astro`

Props: `lang: Lang`.

Sticky at the top, background `--color-glass`, `backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.4)`,
`border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-line)`. Height 64px — the same number the
anchor-scroll offset uses, so define it once as a CSS variable (`--nav-h`) and read it
from both places.

**Left**: the ✳ glyph + `site.name`.
**Right**: four anchor links, the language toggle, the theme toggle.

### 2. Anchor links

`navAbout` → `#about`, `navWork` → `#work`, `navProjects` → `#projects`,
`navContact` → `#contact`.

**None of those sections exist yet** — they arrive with issues 08 to 13. The links ship
anyway, and the smooth-scroll handler must no-op when the target is missing rather than
throw. Do not create placeholder sections to make the links resolve.

Click → `scrollTo({ behavior: 'smooth' })` at the element's offset minus `--nav-h`.
`#top` scrolls to 0 with no offset. With `reduce`, jump without smoothing.

Hidden below 720px. No mobile menu is designed: the toggles stay, the links disappear.

### 3. Language toggle

Moves here from the page scaffold, unchanged in behavior: a real `<a>` to
`siblingPath(pathname, otherLang)` that writes `localStorage.lang` on click. Label is
the language pair, active one emphasized (`ES / en`).

Base's inline script already owns the click handler that persists the choice; keep that
wiring rather than duplicating it.

### 4. Theme toggle

A `<button>` with a half-filled circle icon (CSS, not an image): a circle where half is
`currentColor` and half is transparent, rotated to read as a moon/sun hybrid.

`aria-label` from a new key — **`content.json` has no key for it and is read-only**, so
the label goes in `src/lib/ui.ts` as `{ es: {...}, en: {...} }` alongside `site`. Same
rationale as `site`: UI chrome, not translatable page copy. Ship both languages.

`aria-pressed` reflects dark mode. On click, `toggleTheme()` and update `aria-pressed`.
The button reads its initial state from `document.documentElement.dataset.theme`, which
Base's inline script has already set before first paint — never from `matchMedia`
directly, or the button and the page can disagree.

### 5. `src/lib/motion/scramble.ts` + math

The pure frame function goes in `math.ts`, the timing driver in `scramble.ts`.

```ts
// math.ts
scrambleFrame(target: string, p: number, rand?: () => number): string
```

- Glyph pool: `<>/_-=+*#%&{}[]|\01`
- Resolved prefix length: `n = Math.floor(p ** 2 * target.length)` — quadratic, so it
  resolves left to right and accelerates.
- Characters past `n` are replaced by a random glyph; **spaces are always preserved**,
  resolved or not.
- `rand` is injectable so tests are deterministic. Defaults to `Math.random`.

```ts
// scramble.ts
scramble(el: HTMLElement, duration: number): void
```

# 05 · Hero — spec

Issue: [PV3-10](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-10) · Branch: `feat/05-hero`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.2 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §2 · `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-portfolio-v3-design.md` §6

## Goal

The left column of the hero and the boot sequence that reveals it. The right column —
the console — is issue 06 and stays empty here; the grid already accounts for it.

## Context

`Base.astro` renders `Nav` in its `nav` slot and a scaffold content block in the default
slot. That scaffold block is replaced by the hero.

Available: `content.ts`, `ui.ts`, `theme.ts`, `motion/{math,scroll,scramble,reduced}.ts`.

Hero copy keys: `eyebrow`, `h1a`, `h1b`, `heroSub`, `ctaWork`, `ctaContact`,
`statYears`, `statCompanies`, `statPlatforms`.

## Scope

### 0. Refactor first: shared anchor handling

Nav currently owns the smooth-scroll click handler in its own script. The hero's CTAs
need the same behavior, so **extract it before adding the hero**:

`src/lib/motion/anchors.ts` — binds one delegated `click` listener on `document` for
`[data-nav-link]`, applying the `--nav-h` offset, the `#top` special case, the
missing-target no-op, and the `reduce` guard. Called once from `Base.astro`.

Nav keeps `data-nav-link` on its links and loses its handler. The hero's CTAs get the
same attribute. One handler, one behavior, no duplication — this is why it moves rather
than getting copied.

### 1. `src/components/Hero.astro`

Props: `lang: Lang`.

Grid: `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 380px), 1fr))`. One column below that width,
console under the text.

Padding: `clamp(72px, 10vw, 140px)` top, `clamp(64px, 8vw, 110px)` bottom. This appears
once in the site, so it stays local — not a utility.

Left column, in order:

1. **Eyebrow** — mono, `--text-label`, typed character by character with a permanent
   blinking cursor (7×12px, `blink 1s steps(1) infinite`).
2. **H1** — two lines: `h1a`, then `h1b` in `--color-accent` with
   `text-shadow: 0 0 40px` accent at .3–.45 alpha. `text-wrap: balance`, `--text-h1`.
3. **Sub** — `heroSub`, `--text-hero-sub`, `--color-dim`.
4. **CTAs** — primary filled with `--color-ink` (label `ctaWork` → `#work`), secondary
   outlined (label `ctaContact` → `#contact`). Pills, `border-radius: 999px`. Both carry
   `data-nav-link`. Hover: primary `translateY(-1px)`, secondary border → accent.

# 06 · Decorative console — spec

Issue: [PV3-11](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-11) · Branch: `feat/06-console`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.2 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §2 · `handoff/content.json` → `consoleLog`

## Goal

Fill the hero's empty right column with the orchestration console, in its decorative
form. It also exposes the per-line callback that issue 07 uses to fire node-network
pulses.

The interactive console of `handoff/AGENT_CONSOLE_SPEC.md` is v1.1 and out of scope.

## Context

`Hero.astro` renders an empty `<div>` as the second grid track — the console replaces it.
`boot.ts` already handles `[data-boot]`, and the resting state in `app.css` is shared;
the console overrides only its own transform and duration.

`consoleLog` in `content.json` is 11 `[key, value]` pairs, language-independent.

## Scope

### 1. `src/components/Console.astro`

Card: `--color-console-bg`, `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)`, `border-radius: 28px`,
`box-shadow: 0 30px 80px` at .12 light / .6 dark, 1px border in `--color-line`.

Three parts:

- **Header** — three dots, the label `orchestrator — session 0x4D41`, and a LIVE
  indicator (accent dot + `LIVE`, mono, `--text-label-sm`). This is chrome, not page
  copy: it goes in `ui.ts`, same as the theme-toggle label.
- **Log** — six line slots, each `hh:mm:ss · key · value`, mono ~12.5px. `key` in
  `--color-accent`, `value` in `--color-ink`, time in `--color-dim`. Subtle scanlines
  over the log area (repeating-linear-gradient, very low alpha).
- **Footer** — three metrics: AGENTS, SPECS, SHIPPED. Mono 10px labels with `.12em`
  tracking, 20px values, SHIPPED's value in accent. Separated by 1px borders.

### 2. Timestamps must be client-side

The site is statically built. Rendering `hh:mm:ss` at build time would bake **one
timestamp into the HTML forever** — every visitor would see the moment the site was
deployed, and it would drift further from reality with every day the build is not
redeployed.

So: the server renders the six lines with their `key` and `value` and an **empty time
cell**. JavaScript fills the times as lines cycle. With no JavaScript the log reads as
six key/value lines and no clock, which is honest — better than a frozen wrong time.

### 3. Log cycling — `src/lib/motion/consoleLog.ts`

A new line every 1400ms, `rise .35s` on entry (`opacity 0 → 1`,
`translateY(6px) → 0`). At most six visible: the oldest drops as the newest enters.
The source cycles the 11 messages with `tick % 11`, so it loops forever.

The initial six lines are the first six of the cycle, so the server-rendered markup and
the first client frame agree.

### 4. Metrics — pure, in `math.ts`

Exactly the mock's formulas (`Portfolio.dc.html:696`):

```ts
metricsAt(tick: number): { agents: number; specs: number; shipped: number }
// agents  = 3 + (tick % 2)
// specs   = 12 + Math.floor(tick / 11)
// shipped = 41 + Math.floor(tick / 6)
```

Unit-tested, including that `agents` stays within 3–4 for any tick, and that `specs` and
`shipped` never decrease.

### 5. Boot and sweep

`data-boot="10"` → 2200ms, which `bootDelay` already returns. The console's own resting
state overrides the shared one: `translateY(24px) scale(.96) blur(10px)`, transition
1100ms.

A scan line crosses the card once: 2px tall, accent gradient with a glow,
`sweep 1.4s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1)` with a 1.1s delay, `animation-iteration-count: 1`.
The `sweep` keyframe already exists in `app.css`.

### 6. The callback for issue 07

```ts
export function onLogLine(fn: (line: { key: string; value: string }) => void): () => void
```

Same shape as `onScroll`: subscribe, get an unsubscribe back. Fires exactly once per new
line. Issue 07 subscribes to trigger a network pulse; nothing subscribes yet in this
block, and the API must work with zero subscribers.

### 7. Accessibility — deliberate deviation

`handoff/AGENT_CONSOLE_SPEC.md` asks for `role="log"` with `aria-live="polite"`. That is
right for the **interactive** console of v1.1, where output answers a user action.

Here the log auto-cycles forever with no user input. `aria-live="polite"` would make a
screen reader announce a new line every 1.4 seconds, indefinitely — hostile, and it would
bury the rest of the page.

So this block ships `role="log"` with **`aria-live="off"`** and a comment explaining why.
v1.1 flips it to `polite` when lines become responses to a question. The decorative log
is presentational; nothing in it is information the visitor needs.

### 8. Reduced motion

Six static lines, no cycling, no sweep, no rise. Metrics render at `tick = 0`. The
timestamps stay empty, since nothing drives them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: `metricsAt(tick)` matches the three formulas exactly, for tick 0, 1, 6, 11, 12, 66.
- [ ] `bun test`: `agents` ∈ {3, 4} for every tick in 0..500; `specs` and `shipped` are non-decreasing.
- [ ] `bun test`: the cycle emits the 11 messages in order and wraps, never showing more than six lines.
- [ ] `bun test`: `onLogLine` fires exactly once per line, and the cycle runs fine with zero subscribers.
- [ ] `bun test`: unsubscribing stops delivery; the last unsubscribe stops the interval.
- [ ] `bun test`: with `reduce`, no interval is started.
- [ ] `dist/*.html` contains no `hh:mm:ss` timestamp — the time cells ship empty.
- [ ] The six initial lines in the HTML are the first six of the cycle.
- [ ] `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"`; the LIVE dot and the three header dots are `aria-hidden`.
- [ ] Console chrome copy comes from `ui.ts`, log content from `content.json`. No literal strings in the component.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled: the card renders complete, six lines with key and value, metrics at their base values.
- [ ] Still exactly one scroll listener call site, and one delegated anchor handler.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

The interactive agent (v1.1): input, streaming, expand mode, suggestion chips. The node
canvas (issue 07) — this block only exposes the callback it will consume.

# 07 · Node network canvas — spec

Issue: [PV3-12](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-12) · Branch: `feat/07-network-canvas`
Design: `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §3, §13 · `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html`

## Goal

The hero's background: 84 nodes on a rotating 3D ellipsoid, converging into the ✳ on
load, wired to the console, reacting to the cursor, and collapsing on scroll.

This is the heaviest block in the project. It is also the one where the math/DOM split
pays off most: nearly all of it is testable without a browser.

## Context

`Hero.astro` renders inside `container-page` (max-width 1200px). The canvas is
**full-bleed** and must escape that. Restructure: the hero `<section>` becomes
`position: relative` and full-width, with an inner `container-page` wrapper holding the
two columns. The canvas is a direct child of the section, `position: absolute; inset: 0`.

Stacking: the aurora is `z-index: 0` fixed in `Base`, page content sits in a `z-[1]`
wrapper. Inside that wrapper the hero creates its own stacking context, so the canvas
takes `z-index: 0` and the columns `z-index: 1` — canvas above the aurora, below the
text, no negative z-indexes anywhere.

Already available and **to be reused, not reimplemented**: `onScroll` (`scroll.ts`),
`onLogLine` (`consoleLog.ts`), `prefersReducedMotion` (`reduced.ts`), `math.ts`.

## Scope

### 1. Pure math — `src/lib/motion/math.ts`

Everything below is a pure function with unit tests and no DOM. Anything random takes an
injectable `rand` so tests are deterministic.

```ts
ellipsoidPoint(theta, phi, r: {rx, ry, rz}): {x, y, z}
projectNode(p: {x,y,z}, cam: {f, w, h}): {x, y, sc, depth}
asteriskTarget(i: number, total: number, radius: number): {x, y}
formationPhase(t: number): {mode: 'idle'|'forming'|'holding'|'dissolving', p: number}
connectionAlpha(dist: number, minDepth: number, dark: boolean): number
collapseFactor(scrollY: number, vh: number): number
commandHopDelay(hop: number): number       // -(hop + 1) * .55
nodeCountFor(width: number): number        // 84 desktop, 48 under 720px
```

Values, straight from `MOTION_SPEC` §3:

- Ellipsoid radii: `RX = .56W`, `RY = .48H`, `RZ = .5·min(W,H)`.
- Perspective: `f = .9·max(W,H)`, `sc = f / (f + z)`, `depth ∈ [.3, 1]` drives size and alpha.
- Connections: distance `< 150px`, alpha `(1 - d/150) · .22` dark, `· .28` light, times `min(depth)`.
- ✳: 6 arms, `R = .26·min(W,H)`, centered on the console. Timeline: converge 300→1200ms
  with an ease-in-out cubic, hold to 1900, dissolve 1900→2800.
- Collapse: `clamp(scrollY / (.75·vh), 0, 1)`.

### 2. The canvas class — `src/lib/motion/network.ts`

One class, no dependencies. Owns the canvas element, the node array, and the rAF loop.
It reads `math.ts` for every formula; it must contain **no arithmetic worth testing**.

- Sizing: `devicePixelRatio` capped at 2. Resize is driven by the existing `onScroll`
  subscription's `vh`/resize tick — do **not** add a `resize` listener.
- Loop: rAF with a 24ms throttle (30–40fps target).
- `aria-hidden="true"`, `pointer-events: none`.
- `mask-image: linear-gradient(180deg, #000 55%, transparent)`.

Per-node state: `theta`, `phi`, `dTheta ∈ ±.0005`, latitude oscillation bouncing at
`±1.4 rad`, vertical `sin` of ±9px. Global rotation `.00003 rad/frame`.

### 3. Console wiring

Four anchors on the card's edges: left 25%, left 62%, bottom 50%, top 30%. Each connects
to the nearest visible node within 280px, skipping nodes occluded by the card.

The card rect is read **once per resize**, cached — never per frame.

Every log line (`onLogLine`) fires a command: a pulse from the left-62% anchor, then a
**BFS of 3 hops** through the connection graph. Hop `n` is delayed by `commandHopDelay(n)`,
travels at `.045` per frame with a `.18` tail. On arrival the node flashes: a ring growing
to 22px, decaying `×.93` per frame.

Commands stop firing once `collapse ≥ .6`.

### 4. Cursor

A violet node with a glow. Attracts nodes within 200px with force `(1 - d/200) · 1.4`,
decaying `×.9`. Violet lines to nodes within 170px. Nearby connections gain `+.35` alpha.
The pointer tilts the camera: `tilt ±.25 rad`, `rot ±.15`.

Desktop only. On touch, no cursor node and no attraction — bind on `pointermove` with
`pointerType === 'mouse'` rather than sniffing the user agent.

### 5. Scroll collapse

From the existing `onScroll` subscription: radius `×(1 - .85·collapse)`, rotation
`×(1 + 5·collapse)`, `globalAlpha = 1 - collapse`. At `collapse >= 1` the loop parks
itself — no drawing while the canvas is invisible — and resumes when it drops below 1.

### 6. Performance

Budget: ≤4ms per frame on an M1 (`MOTION_SPEC` §13). Mobile starts at 48 nodes.

Degradation: sample frame times over the first 60 frames; if the median exceeds 33ms,
drop to 40 nodes **once** and stop sampling. No adaptive loop that could oscillate.

### 7. Reduced motion

The canvas is **not created at all** — no element in the DOM, no rAF, no subscriptions.
Assert the absence of the element, not just that it is invisible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun test`: `projectNode` returns known values for a node at the front, at the back, and at the edge, including that `sc` shrinks as `z` grows.
- [ ] `bun test`: `ellipsoidPoint` puts every point on the ellipsoid surface — `(x/rx)² + (y/ry)² + (z/rz)² ≈ 1` for a sweep of angles.
- [ ] `bun test`: `asteriskTarget` distributes `total` nodes across exactly 6 arms, all within `radius`, symmetric about the center.
- [ ] `bun test`: `formationPhase` returns the right mode and a 0→1 progress at t = 0, 300, 750, 1200, 1900, 2350, 2800 and beyond.
- [ ] `bun test`: `connectionAlpha` is 0 at exactly 150px, maximum at 0px, and higher in light than dark for the same distance.
- [ ] `bun test`: `collapseFactor` is 0 at 0, 1 at `.75·vh`, and clamps above.
- [ ] `bun test`: the BFS visits at most 3 hops, never repeats a node, and terminates on a disconnected graph.
- [ ] `bun test`: `commandHopDelay(n) === -(n + 1) * .55`.
- [ ] `bun test`: `nodeCountFor` gives 84 at 1440px and 48 at 600px.
- [ ] With `reduce`: no `<canvas>` element exists in the DOM.
- [ ] Still exactly one scroll listener call site and one delegated anchor handler; the canvas adds neither a `scroll` nor a `resize` listener.
- [ ] The canvas is `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none`, and sits behind the hero text.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled the hero is unaffected — the canvas simply never appears.
- [ ] Measured frame time stays within budget at 84 nodes; report the actual number.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` pass.

## Out of scope

Every section below the hero. The interactive console (v1.1) — this block consumes
`onLogLine` as it already exists and does not change it.

`07` lista. PR: **https://github.com/djmaam/portfolio-v3/pull/8** — CI corriendo.

**0,30 ms de mediana por frame** contra un presupuesto de 4 ms, medido en Chrome headless real sobre ~190 frames a 84 nodos. El subagente aclara honestamente que es tiempo de callback de rAF en el main thread — la rasterización GPU no está incluida —, pero es exactamente la métrica de la que habla `MOTION_SPEC` §13.

Dos cosas del bloque que valen más que el canvas en sí:

**Leer los tokens desde el canvas necesitó un rodeo.** `getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('--color-accent')` devuelve el `light-dark(#…, #…)` sin resolver, que a un canvas no le sirve para nada. La solución: el elemento lleva `color: var(--color-accent)` y `border-color: var(--color-violet)` con ancho 0, y la clase lee `styles.color` de vuelta ya resuelto. Un `MutationObserver` sobre `data-theme` los re-lee al cambiar de tema.

**El lint anti-hex forzó una implementación más rápida.** `check-tokens` rechaza cualquier `rgba(` literal fuera de `app.css`, así que la técnica del mock —armar un string de color por línea dibujada— quedaba prohibida. Terminó seteando `strokeStyle` una vez por grupo y modulando `ctx.globalAlpha`, que es buena parte de por qué el frame time dio tan bajo. Una regla de estilo que salió barata en performance.

Y el costo real de "nada de aritmética en la clase": **19 funciones en `math.ts`**, no las 8 que yo había listado. En la clase quedó solo `Math.hypot` dentro de los loops de dibujo y una combinación de alfas.

The first section below the hero, and the generic reveal observer that issues 10 to 13
all consume. That shared module is the more important half of this block.

## Context

`Base.astro` renders `Nav` and the page content. The hero is the only section so far.

`onScroll` (`scroll.ts`) already delivers `{ scrollY, vh, progress }` once per frame to
any subscriber. About's word illumination hooks onto it — **it must not add a listener**.

### 1. `src/lib/motion/reveal.ts` — shared, used by 10-13

An `IntersectionObserver` that reveals `[data-reveal]` elements once:

- Initial state (only under `html.has-js` and `no-preference`):
  `opacity: 0; transform: translateY(18px); filter: blur(6px)`.
- Transition 800ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`.
- Observer: `threshold: .15`, `rootMargin: '0px 0px -8% 0px'`, unobserve after firing.
- `data-delay` in ms staggers the transition.

```ts
export function bindReveals(root?: ParentNode): () => void
```

Called once from `Base.astro`, like `bindAnchors`. Under `reduce` it returns a no-op and
never constructs the observer.

**Rule from `MOTION_SPEC` §5, and it matters:** `data-reveal` goes on a *wrapper*, never
on the element that also has a hover `transform`. Two transforms on one element fight.
Enforce it in review, and follow it in the markup here.

The resting-state CSS lives in `app.css` next to the `[data-boot]` rule, for the same
reason: it is shared, and cascade order against a scoped style should not be
load-bearing.

Props: `lang: Lang`. Section `id="about"` — the nav link finally resolves.

Layout: mono label `01 / SOBRE MÍ` on the left, content on the right at roughly 2/3.
Uses `container-page`, `section-y` and `section-divider`.

1. **Lead** — `aboutLead` at `--text-lead`, split into words:
   `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0 .26em`. Each word starts at `opacity: .16`
   with a 350ms transition.

   `<li>` and the transform lives on the inner card.

```ts

wordOpacity(index: number, total: number, p: number): number  // clamp(p·(total+3) - index, .16, 1)
```

Tres PRs abiertas: **#11 (Experiencia)**, **#12 (Proyectos)**, **#13 (Stack)**. Falta Contacto, que sigue corriendo.

Lo más valioso del round no fue el código sino dos cosas que los agentes cazaron y yo no había visto:

**El Stack encontró un bug en el mock.** Las marquesinas usan `gap` de flex entre chips. Con `gap`, el track de dos mitades mide `2 × mitad + gap`, así que el `translateX(-50%)` se queda corto por medio gap y el loop **salta visiblemente una vez por ciclo**. Está en el mock y se hubiera copiado tal cual. La solución fue mover los 8px a `margin-inline-end` del chip: ahí el track mide exactamente dos mitades y la costura es perfecta.

**El estado de `reduce` del Stack estaba mal planteado en mi spec.** Yo pedí "filas estáticas y legibles". Estático solo hubiera dejado la fila cortada por el `overflow: hidden` con unos 40 de los 52 chips inalcanzables — cumplía "estático" y fallaba "legible". El agente hizo que bajo `reduce` la fila haga `flex-wrap: wrap` con el clon oculto, así se ven todos.

Y el `check-tokens` que escribimos en la `01` mordió de una forma que no había previsto: **escanea comentarios**. El agente de Experiencia escribió un comentario explicando la trampa de `dot`/`glow` y citó los dos colores literales — el linter lo rechazó. Tuvo que describirlos en vez de citarlos.

## How the icons were verified

- In `dist/_astro/*.css` each pill icon is `.icon[data-icon=github|linkedin|telegram]{mask-image:url("data:image/svg+xml,…")}` over a shared `.icon{background:currentColor;mask-position:50%;mask-size:contain;mask-repeat:no-repeat}`. Color therefore comes only from `currentColor`, which is `--color-contact-ink` inherited from the card (so it inverts with the theme) and becomes `--color-contact-accent` on `.pill:hover` — the same element, one property, both states.
- I decoded the three data URIs out of the built CSS and diffed each `d` against a freshly fetched upstream file: `path identical to upstream = True` for all three, and `'fill' in data uri = False` for all three (the SVGs carry no `fill`, no `color`, no `currentColor` — the default opaque black is only ever read as mask alpha). The only `fill` left anywhere in the bundle is Tailwind's `transition-property` list.
- Other build checks: `.card{background:var(--color-contact-card);color:var(--color-contact-ink)}` with both tokens emitted as `light-dark()` pairs that are the theme's own colors swapped (inverted in light and dark alike); all three social anchors carry `target="_blank" rel="noopener"` and the email is a bare `mailto:`; every `animation:` in the bundle — `spin 7s` and `gridflow 6s` included — sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference)`; `[data-reveal]` hides only under `.has-js`, so the card is complete without JS; `grep` over `src/` still finds exactly one `addEventListener('scroll'` call site (`src/lib/motion/scroll.ts`).

Files touched: `src/components/Contact.astro` (new), `tests/contact.test.ts` (new), `src/styles/app.css` (+6 lines), and only the two `contact` markers in `src/pages/index.astro` / `src/pages/en/index.astro`. The other four markers are asserted intact by a test.

## Decisions the spec did not cover

1. **One new token, `--color-contact-accent: light-dark(#3ee7ff, #0a8faf)`.** Not for the card/ink inversion (I used the existing pair for that) but for the accent inside the card: `#3ee7ff` on the light card is ~1.35:1 and disappears, so the label, the email and the pill hover need `--color-accent` with its branches swapped. I first scoped it as `.contact-card { --color-accent: … }` to avoid a new name — that broke `tests/tokens.test.ts`, which maps every `--name:` in `app.css` by name and would then see two declarations of `--color-accent`. Since that test isn't mine to edit, the swapped value got its own name next to the other two. The beam and halo stay on the page's own `--color-accent`/`--color-violet`, as in the mock.
2. **Icon sources.** GitHub and Telegram are Simple Icons verbatim; LinkedIn is `mdi/linkedin` (Simple Icons dropped the LinkedIn mark) — the same source the mock itself pointed at. Inlined as paths, so no dependency and no runtime request; the mock's CDN URLs would have been a third-party fetch.
3. **No brand string is copy.** `content.json` has no `GITHUB`/`LINKEDIN`/`TELEGRAM`, so the pills iterate the `links` keys and upper-case them for the label. Adding a key to `links` grows the row; only the icon has to be drawn.
4. **Borders and the grid mask use `currentColor`/`color-mix`, not tokens** (`color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 20%, transparent)` for pill borders, `currentColor` as the opaque end of the radial mask, where only alpha matters). They invert with the card for free.
5. **Two sizes stayed local instead of becoming tokens**, both used once: the email's `clamp(22px, 2.9vw, 34px)` (the mock's `cqw` converted the way the existing tokens were) and the card padding, whose floor I lowered from the mock's 36px to 28px so a 320px screen keeps some line length inside `container-page`'s own 20px.
6. **No `<script>` in the component.** `Base.astro` already calls `bindReveals()` over the whole document, so the section only ships `data-reveal`; a second call would double-observe.
7. **Not done, deliberately:** no custom focus ring. `DESIGN_SPEC` §4 asks for one on everything interactive and notes it is absent from the mock — nothing in the repo implements it yet, so it belongs to a site-wide pass rather than to this card, and the default UA outline is untouched in the meantime.
8. **Worth knowing:** lightningcss emitted the icon masks unprefixed (it only prefixed the pre-existing `.hero-net` gradient mask), so the icons need Safari 15.4+ / any current browser. I left the output as the toolchain produced it rather than hand-writing `-webkit-` copies.</result>

content.text:
Cuatro PRs abiertas — **#11** Experiencia, **#12** Proyectos, **#13** Stack, **#14** Contacto. CI corriendo en las cuatro.

El hallazgo del bloque de Contacto merece atención porque es un bug de accesibilidad real que mi spec no vio venir:

**La tarjeta invierte el tema, y el acento no seguía la inversión.** En modo claro la tarjeta es oscura, pero `--color-accent` resuelve a su rama clara (`#0a8faf`) contra ese fondo oscuro. Y al revés: en modo oscuro, `#3ee7ff` sobre una tarjeta casi blanca da **1.35:1** de contraste — el texto prácticamente desaparece. Ahora la etiqueta, el email y el hover de los pills usan `--color-contact-accent`, con las ramas intercambiadas. El haz giratorio y el halo siguen con el acento normal de la página, como en el mock.

Fijate también que el agente probó los iconos en serio: decodificó los tres data URI del CSS construido y comparó cada `path` contra el archivo original de Simple Icons. Iguales, y ninguno con `fill` — el negro por defecto del SVG solo se lee como alfa de máscara.

Tres agentes distintos, en paralelo, flaggearon lo mismo por su cuenta: **falta el anillo de foco**. `DESIGN_SPEC` §4 lo pide en todo lo interactivo y aclara que no está en el mock. Es exactamente el issue `16`, y ahora tengo tres confirmaciones independientes de que hace falta.

cat > docs/superpowers/specs/09-method.md <<'EOF'
# 09 · How I work — spec

Issue: [PV3-14](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-14) · Branch: `feat/09-method`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.4 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §7 · `handoff/README.md` rule 6

## Goal

The last section, and the one with the most state logic in the site: a pinned block whose
five cards light up in sequence as the page scrolls past it.

## Context

Every other section is merged. Both pages still carry the `method` markers — the only
pair left. The section lands between About and Experience, which is where the markers
already sit.

Reuse, do not reimplement: `onScroll` (`scroll.ts`), `bindReveals` (`reveal.ts`),
`prefersReducedMotion` (`reduced.ts`).

Content: `secMethod`, `methodTitle`, `methodSub`, `cycleIdle`, `cycleDone`,
`stepVerbs` (a **pipe-separated string** of 5 verbs, not an array), `steps`
(5 × `{n, color, h, d, tool}`).

## Scope

### 1. Colors come from tokens, never from the JSON

`steps[].color` holds the five traffic-light hexes. Unlike the experience `dot`/`glow`
trap, these *are* real design colors — and they already exist as `--color-step-1`
through `--color-step-5`, added in issue 01. Map step index → token. Do not emit the
literal, and do not add new tokens.

### 2. `src/components/Method.astro`

Props: `lang: Lang`. Section `id="method"`.

Header: mono `02 / CÓMO TRABAJO` + `methodTitle` + `methodSub`, plus the status indicator
(a dot and a mono line) on the right.

Five cards in a grid `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 150px), 1fr))` — five across from
about 850px. Each card: `n`, a dot, `h`, `d`, and `tool` at the foot behind a
`border-top: 1px dashed`.

### 3. The pinned track

Desktop, **and only when both** the viewport is at least 720px wide **and** the block fits
in the viewport height: the section gets a 280vh track containing a
`position: sticky; top: 0; min-height: 100vh` block, vertically centered, 32px padding.

Progress: `p = -track.top / (track.height - vh)`.

Mobile or a block that does not fit: no sticky at all,
`p = (.85·vh - top) / (.9·height)`, same step logic.

The fit test runs on resize (through the existing `onScroll` tick — **no new listener**)
and toggles a class, so rotating a phone does not strand the section half-pinned.

### 4. Step state — pure math

```ts
methodStep(p: number): { active: number; done: boolean }
// active = p < .06 ? -1 : Math.min(4, Math.floor((p - .06) / .84 * 5))
// done   = p >= .93
methodProgress(top: number, height: number, vh: number, pinned: boolean): number
```

Both in `math.ts`, unit-tested. `MOTION_SPEC` §7 exactly.

Card states:

| state | style |
|---|---|
| upcoming | `opacity: .22; transform: translateY(10px) scale(.97)`, `--color-line` border |
| active | `translateY(-6px) scale(1.03)`, border and `0 0 0 1px` ring in its own step color, `0 20px 60px` shadow |
| completed | normal, dot lit in its step color at `scale(1.25)` with a `0 0 12px` glow |
| done (all) | accent border at .65, `--color-accent-soft` background, `0 0 44px` accent glow, accent dots |

Transitions 600ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`, and **reversible**: scrolling back up walks
the states backwards. The state is a pure function of `p`, so this falls out for free —
do not accumulate state across frames.

### 5. Status indicator

`cycleIdle` → `${verb} · ${n}/5` for each of the five verbs → `cycleDone`.

The verbs come from `stepVerbs.split('|')`, which must yield exactly 5. Assert it: a
missing pipe would silently shift every label by one.

The dot and the text take the active step's color; at `done` they take the accent.

# 16 · Accessibility pass — spec

Issue: [PV3-21](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-21) · Branch: `feat/16-a11y`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §4, §6 · `handoff/README.md` rule 5

## Goal

The first block that reads the whole site at once. Every section was built in isolation,
so this is where cross-component inconsistencies surface.

## Context

Every section is merged. The site has ten components, two routes, two themes, and a
`reduce` mode.

**The focus ring is missing.** `DESIGN_SPEC` §4 asks for a `2px accent` ring with a 2px
offset on everything interactive, and notes it is absent from the mock. Three separate
agents flagged it while building their sections and correctly left it alone as
cross-cutting work. Today `src/components/Projects.astro` has the site's only
`:focus-visible` rule.

## Scope

### 1. Global focus ring

One rule in `app.css`:

```css
:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

`:focus-visible`, not `:focus` — a mouse click on a button must not leave a ring behind.

**The inverted contact card is the exception that proves the rule.** `--color-accent`
inside it resolves against an inverted background, exactly the contrast bug issue 13
found. Inside the card the ring uses `--color-contact-accent`.

Remove the local rule from `Projects.astro` once the global one covers it — a duplicate
that drifts is worse than none.

### 2. Contrast, as a permanent test

Do not eyeball this and do not check it once by hand. `src/styles/app.css` holds every
color as a `light-dark(a, b)` pair, so the ratios can be computed:

`tests/contrast.test.ts` parses the tokens out of `app.css`, computes the WCAG 2.1
relative-luminance ratio for each pair below, and asserts the threshold **in both
themes**:

| foreground | background | minimum |
|---|---|---|
| `ink` | `bg` | 4.5 |
| `dim` | `bg` | 4.5 |
| `dim` | `surface` over `bg` | 4.5 |
| `accent` | `bg` | 3.0 (large/medium text only — see below) |
| `contact-ink` | `contact-card` | 4.5 |
| `contact-accent` | `contact-card` | 4.5 |

`DESIGN_SPEC` §6 allows accent as text only at ≥15px or weight 500, which is the
large-text threshold of 3:1. The test encodes that, and a second assertion greps the
components: any rule setting `color: var(--color-accent)` must also set a
`font-size` ≥ 15px or a `font-weight` ≥ 500 in the same block. If a component violates
it, fix the component, not the test.

This is a test rather than an audit because tokens will change again.

### 3. ARIA and semantics audit

Verify across all ten components, and fix what is wrong:

- Toggles carry `aria-label` and, where they express a binary state, `aria-pressed`.
- Decorative glyphs (✳, the ASCIImoji, the console dots, the step dots) are `aria-hidden`.
- The canvas is `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events: none`.
- Preview iframes are `aria-hidden` and `tabindex="-1"` — never a tab stop.
- The duplicated marquee halves are `aria-hidden`, so each technology is read once.
- The console log is `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` (issue 06 §7 explains why, and

- One `<h1>` per page. Section headings descend without skipping a level.
- Every `<section>` with an id has an accessible name.

### 4. Keyboard traversal

Tab through both routes and confirm: order follows the visual order, focus is always
visible, nothing traps it, and every interactive element is reachable. The nav is sticky,
so also confirm a focused element never lands underneath it — `scroll-margin-top` was

export type PreviewMode = 'screenshot'

Closes PV3-22.

The end-to-end safety net and the performance budget. Small on purpose — 305 unit tests already cover every formula, the contrast ratios and the a11y invariants, so this block only proves the DOM plumbing runs in a real browser.

## Verification

```
bun run lint      → passes
bun test          → 305 pass, 0 fail
bun run build     → 2 pages built
bunx playwright   → 7 passed (5.5s), three consecutive runs, no flake
```

**Lighthouse, mobile, 3 runs per page, both routes:**

| | Performance | Accessibility | Best Practices | SEO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | **1.00** | 0.96 | **1.00** | **1.00** |
| `/en` | **1.00** | 0.96 | **1.00** | **1.00** |

## The focus-ring test closes issue 16's open item

Issue 16 could not verify whether the ring is *visually* clipped — that is layout geometry, not structure, and it needs a browser. Test 7 tabs to all 21 focusable elements, expands each rect by the 2px ring plus its 2px offset, and asserts it fits inside every `overflow: hidden` ancestor.

**It found no defect.** More importantly, it was proven to bite: adding `overflow: hidden` to Contact's `.reach` — whose padding box is flush with the email — made it fail with four named elements, *while the elements themselves still fit*. Only the ring crossed the boundary, which is the exact defect class. Reverted, green again. A test that cannot fail is worse than no test.

## Two real defects fixed along the way

**`loading="lazy"` was not deferring anything.** The Projects markup promised in its own comment that iframes never load before being scrolled to. Measured under Pixel 5 emulation: 50 external requests fired with zero scrolling, with the section 5700px away. Chrome applies a large margin on fast connections.

**The previews are now static screenshots** — all six, your call after I laid out the tradeoff. Four live cross-origin embeds dragged 40–50 third-party requests into the page (Tag Manager, Wix, Cloudflare Insights) plus third-party-cookie penalties, costing `/en` Performance 0.82 and Best Practices 0.79. Worse, the `/` vs `/en` gap was not a page difference — the pages are identical — but CDN warmth, which made the budget non-deterministic and would have landed anywhere in cold CI.

The agent measured before touching anything and correctly refused to degrade shimmer, aurora or node count: TBT was 0ms and CLS 0.005, so `MOTION_SPEC` §13's levers would have hurt the design for zero gain. It also refused to lower a threshold.

JPEG rather than PNG: **723 KB across the six against 2.5 MB**, same 960×660 pixels. The iframe path and its `IntersectionObserver` are gone rather than left as dead code, and three tests that asserted iframe behavior were rewritten — including one that now guards against an iframe quietly coming back.

## Known, not a defect

Accessibility sits at 0.96 on both pages, above the 90 threshold. The single failing audit is `color-contrast` on the Method section's **upcoming** step cards, which sit at `opacity: .22` by design (`MOTION_SPEC` §7). Lighthouse measures a static snapshot at load; those cards light up as you scroll, and with `reduce` or with JavaScript disabled they are never dimmed at all. Raising the opacity would contradict the motion spec, so it stays documented rather than "fixed".

## Notes

- **CI**: two jobs in parallel; the critical path is the browser job at ~85s of work plus runner setup. Lighthouse is 90% of it. Comfortably under the 5-minute budget.
- `bunfig.toml` pins `[test] root = "tests"` — Bun's default patterns were picking up `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` and failing it.
- `webServer.env` sets `ASTRO_PREVIEW_BACKGROUND=false`: Astro 7 auto-daemonizes `preview` in agent environments, and Playwright reads the foreground exit as the server dying.
- Two dependencies added, both expected: `@playwright/test` and `@lhci/cli`.

EOF

content.text: Causa clara: LHCI lanza Chrome **sin `--no-sandbox`**, y los runners de Ubuntu tienen restringidos los namespaces de usuario sin privilegios por AppArmor. Playwright pasa porque lanza con sus propios flags; el launcher de Lighthouse no. Es el fallo clásico de Chrome en CI.

input.command: git checkout -q feat/17-e2e-lighthouse && cat lighthouserc.json

python3 - <<'PY'
import json, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('lighthouserc.json')
c = json.loads(p.read_text())
c['ci']['collect']['settings'] = {
    # GitHub's Ubuntu runners restrict unprivileged user namespaces through AppArmor, so
    # Chrome's sandbox cannot start and the launcher dies with "No usable sandbox!".
    # Playwright passes its own flags and is unaffected; Lighthouse launches Chrome
    # itself, so it needs them here. Safe on an ephemeral runner loading only our build.
    'chromeFlags': '--no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage',
}
p.write_text(json.dumps(c, indent=2) + '\n')
PY

Der: **consola** (header con 3 puntos + "orchestrator — session 0x4D41" + LIVE; log de 6 líneas `hh:mm:ss · key · value` con scanlines sutiles; footer 3 métricas AGENTS / SPECS / SHIPPED). Fondo: canvas de red de nodos (ver MOTION) + aurora fija.
3. **01 / Sobre mí**: label a la izquierda, contenido 2/3 a la derecha: lead grande (palabras que se iluminan al scroll), párrafo, 3 principios en tarjetas.

5. **03 / Experiencia**: timeline vertical: riel 1px + dot (el actual en cian con glow), logo 56px (placeholder rayado con abreviatura), empresa + período mono, rol en cian, nota, chips de alcance (mono 11px, radio 8px). Debajo, caja dashed "TAMBIÉN CON" con nombres.

Canvas absoluto, `100vw × 100vh`, `mask-image: linear-gradient(180deg,#000 55%,transparent)`, 30–40 fps (`rAF` con throttle 24ms), `dpr ≤ 2`, debajo del contenido (`z-index` menor que `<main>`).

Rotación global casi nula (`.00003 rad/frame`); cada nodo deriva en su órbita (`dθ ±.0005`, latitud oscila y rebota en ±1.4 rad, `sin` vertical ±9px).

- **Formación ✳** al cargar: 300→1200ms los nodos convergen (ease in-out cúbico) al asterisco de 6 brazos (R = .26·min(W,H)) centrado en la consola; hold hasta 1900; se disuelve 1900→2800 mientras la consola aparece (2200).


Tailwind's reset sets `box-sizing: border-box`, so the 1200px cap **includes** the padding. At a 1512px viewport the content box ends up 1104px wide, starting at x=204.

The mock does the opposite — measured on `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html` at 1512×950:

```
MAIN  max-width: 1200px   padding: 48px   box-sizing: content-box
      border box 1296 wide, content 1200 wide, starting at x=156
```

So every section of the site is **96px narrower and 48px further inward** than the design. That is what makes the H1 wrap to five lines instead of four and the console render 48px too narrow.

## Measured, at 1512×950

| | Mock | Ours | With `content-box` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Content column | 1200 | 1104 | **1200** |
| Content starts at x | 156 | 204 | **156** |
| Hero column | 564 | 516 | **564** |
| H1 width | 564 | 516 | **564** |
| H1 height | 296 (4 lines) | 380 (5 lines) | **304 (4 lines)** |
| Console width | ~562 | 509 | **564** |

Verified in the browser by injecting `.container-page { box-sizing: content-box }` and re-measuring — no other change.

## The fix

Add `box-sizing: content-box` to the `container-page` utility. Check the sections that assume the narrower box (project grid, method steps, contact card) still hold at the wider measure, and re-check the ≤720px end where the padding still has to shrink to 20px.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the built page's content column is 1200px wide at a 1512px viewport, and that it starts at x=156.
- [ ] The hero H1 renders in **four** lines at 1512px, not five.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green; the 7 Playwright tests still pass.
- [ ] Lighthouse still ≥ 0.90 on the four categories (the container change moves CLS-relevant geometry).

## Notes

Depends on nothing. **Blocks 20 and 27** — do not start those until this lands.

input.title: 21 · Nav language toggle renders on two lines
input.description: ## The defect The toggle shows `ES` stacked **above** `/ en` instead of side by side. Root cause is a CSS Grid anonymous-item bug in `Nav.astro`: ```astro {lang.toUpperCase()} / {otherLang} ``` ```css .toggle { display: grid; place-items: center; } .lang { white-space: nowrap; } ``` A grid container wraps every stray text run in an **anonymous grid item**. So `ES` and the text ` / en` become two items, and the default `grid-auto-flow: row` puts them on two rows. `white-space: nowrap` cannot help — they are not on the same line to begin with. Measured: `clientHeight` 34px (the fixed height clips it) against `scrollHeight` **36px** — two 18px lines. ## The fix Any of: make `.toggle` an `inline-flex`, set `grid-auto-flow: column`, or wrap the trailing text in its own span and give the grid one column. Keep the 34px pill height and the `place-items: center` behavior for `.theme`, which is a single-child grid and is fine as is. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A test asserts the lang toggle's `scrollHeight` is not greater than its `clientHeight`, on both `/` and `/en`. - [ ] `ES / en` renders on one line; the pill keeps its 34px height and 999px radius. - [ ] The link is still a real `` with `rel="alternate"` — the no-JS translation path of issue 16 must not regress. - [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green.

input.title: 22 · Stack: the marquee blows the page open, and 4-5 shorter rows
input.description:
Two things in `Stack.astro`: a bug that breaks the whole page, and a design change on top of it.

## Part 1 — the bug: page-wide horizontal scroll

Measured at 1512×950: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` is **3588px** against a 1512px viewport. The mock measures 1512 — no overflow at all.

Root cause: `.stack` is a grid whose single implicit column is sized `auto`, so the track resolves to the **max-content** of its widest item. `.rows` contains `.track { width: max-content; flex-wrap: nowrap }`, which is 3100px of chips. `.row { overflow: hidden }` zeroes the automatic *minimum* size but does nothing to the max-content contribution, so the track grows to 3384px and drags the container, the section and the document with it.

Two visible consequences, both reported:

1. **The subtitle sits at the far end of the horizontal scroll.** `header` is a sibling grid item in the same blown track, so its `auto-fit` two-column grid expands to 3384px and column 2 (`stackSub`) starts at **x=1912** — off screen.
2. **The right-hand fade never shows.** The `mask-image` 8%/92% is symmetric and correct, but 92% of a 3384px row is off screen, so only the left blur is ever visible. This is the "no tiene el blur como en la parte izquierda" report — the mask is fine, the width is not.

A third, quieter one: row 3's track measures 3384px — stretched to the blown row rather than its natural max-content — so `translateX(-50%)` no longer lands on the clone boundary and that row shows a seam once per loop.

**The fix**, verified in the browser: `.stack { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) }` takes `scrollWidth` from 3588 to **1512** and puts the subtitle back at x=772.

## Part 2 — 4-5 rows instead of 3

Design change requested by Marcos, and a **deliberate deviation from the handoff**: `DESIGN_SPEC` §7 and `MOTION_SPEC` §10 both specify three rows at 70s / 85s (reverse) / 78s. With 17-18 chips per row each track runs ~3100px, roughly 2× the viewport, so any given technology is off screen most of the time.

Redistribute the same `stack.rows` content from `handoff/content.json` into **4 or 5 rows**, so each track is closer to one viewport wide and the whole stack reads at a glance. Keep: the marquee, the alternating direction, the pause on hover, the symmetric edge mask, the `● USO A DIARIO / ○ TAMBIÉN HABLO` legend and the highlighted-chip rule. Assign speeds per row in the same 70-85s family, and keep the duplicated-half structure so the loop stays seamless.

`content.json` is read-only — the regrouping belongs in the component or in `src/lib/`, not in the handoff.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts `document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` on `/` and `/en`, at 1512px, 1024px and 390px. This is the guard that keeps any future section from doing the same thing.
- [ ] The stack subtitle is inside the viewport, in the header's second column.
- [ ] Each row's `.track` width equals exactly 2× the width of one `.half`, so `translateX(-50%)` is seamless.
- [ ] 4 or 5 rows; every technology from `stack.rows` appears exactly once per half, none dropped.
- [ ] Both edges fade: a test asserts the mask is symmetric and the row is no wider than its container.
- [ ] With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the rows are static, wrapped and fully readable.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green.

input.title: 23 · Experience: timeline dot off-center, and "también con" stacks vertically
input.description:
Two defects in `Experience.astro`, same file, one PR.

## 1 — The timeline dot is not centered on the company

```css
.dot { margin-top: 28px; }
```

A magic number that does not track what it should line up with. Measured against the card's top edge, identically on all five jobs:

| | Offset from card top |
|---|---|
| Dot center | 34px |
| Logo center | 49px |

**15px off**, on every entry. The dot should sit on the vertical center of the company row — the 56px logo, which starts after the card's 20px padding, so its center is at 48px.

Fix it so it is derived, not guessed: align the dot to `.who` (the logo + name row) rather than offsetting it from the card by hand, so it survives any change to the card padding or the logo size — including issue 15, when the real logos replace the striped placeholder.

## 2 — "TAMBIÉN CON" renders as a vertical list

`DESIGN_SPEC` §5 puts the company names in a horizontal row inside the dashed box. `.also` is a flex row, but `.also-list` inside it has **no rule at all** — it falls back to `display: block`, so the four names stack. Measured: `display: block`, height 96px for 4 items.

Give `.also-list` `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap` with a gap in the family of the `.also` box (14px 28px). It should wrap to a second line on narrow viewports rather than overflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts, for every job, that the dot's vertical center equals the logo's vertical center within 1px.
- [ ] The assertion is derived from the rendered geometry, not from a hardcoded 48px — it has to keep holding when the logos change.
- [ ] A test asserts `.also-list` lays its items out on one line at 1512px, and that its height is one row's worth.
- [ ] The `.also-list` wraps instead of overflowing at 390px, and issue 22's no-horizontal-scroll guard still passes.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green.

## Notes

The `alsoWithCompanies` list in `src/lib/ui.ts` (Creativa Media Lab, Kodai, Hashme, Demedis) is still taken from the mock and **pending Marcos's confirmation**. This issue does not change its contents.

input.title: 24 · Projects: the shimmer cuts off at the right edge and restarts
input.description:
## The defect

The diagonal shimmer over each preview travels, then visibly stops half-visible at the right edge and snaps back to the start. It reads as a cut, not a loop.

`Projects.astro` + `app.css`:

```css
.shimmer { left: -40%; width: 40%; transform: skewX(-12deg); }
.shimmer { animation: shimmer 2.8s ease-in-out infinite; }   /* under no-preference */
@keyframes shimmer { to { transform: translateX(250%); } }
```

The band is 40% of the frame and starts at `left: -40%`, so it is already offscreen-left before any transform. It then travels `translateX(250%)` of its **own** width = 100% of the frame, landing with its left edge at 60% and its **right edge exactly on the frame's right edge**. So the last thing you see is the band parked against the right border — and `ease-in-out` decelerates into precisely that moment — before it teleports back to `-40%`.

`MOTION_SPEC` §9 specifies `translateX(-100% → 250%)`, i.e. the band starts at `left: 0` and is moved offscreen by the transform. With `left: 0`, `translateX(250%)` puts the left edge at 100% of the frame — fully past the right edge, invisible at the moment it wraps. Our `left: -40%` double-counts the initial offset and eats 40% off the end of the travel.

## The fix

Restore the handoff's geometry: `left: 0`, and animate `from { translateX(-100%) } to { translateX(250%) }`. Then confirm the loop actually reads as continuous — with the band fully clear of both edges at the wrap point, the reset is invisible. If a beat between passes is wanted, express it as keyframe percentages (band offscreen from ~70% to 100% of the cycle) rather than leaving the band parked on screen.

`@keyframes shimmer` is shared in `app.css`; check nothing else consumes it before changing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the shimmer's bounding box does not intersect the preview frame at either `0%` or `100%` of the animation — the loop point is invisible by construction.
- [ ] The band still enters from the left, is skewed `-12deg`, is 40% wide, and uses `accent@.12`.
- [ ] The animation stays inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` — the whole-site guard in `tests/a11y.test.ts` must still pass.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green.

input.title: 25 · Telecentro preview: screenshot /t-play, not the root
input.description:
## The ask

`public/previews/telecentro.com.ar.jpg` is a screenshot of `https://telecentro.com.ar/`. It should be **`https://telecentro.com.ar/t-play`** — the product Marcos actually worked on, and what the card's description claims.

## The constraint

`scripts/capture-previews.ts` navigates to `project.url` straight from `handoff/content.json`:

```ts

```

and `content.json` line 176 / 391 has `"url": "https://telecentro.com.ar/"` for both languages. **`handoff/` is read-only** (`CLAUDE.md`), so the URL cannot be edited there.

The card's outgoing link is a separate decision from what gets screenshotted, so they need to stop being the same value. Add a host-keyed shot-URL override next to the existing `PREVIEWS` table in `src/lib/projects.ts` — that file already owns the host-keyed preview policy, and keying by host (never by index) is the rule that survives a reordered `content.json`. `capture-previews.ts` then reads the override and falls back to `project.url`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the shot URL resolved for `telecentro.com.ar` is `https://telecentro.com.ar/t-play`, and that every other project falls back to its `content.json` URL.
- [ ] The override is keyed by host, and a test asserts reversing `content.es.projects` does not change any resolved shot URL.
- [ ] `bun scripts/capture-previews.ts telecentro.com.ar` regenerates the JPEG; it is committed, still 960×660, quality 82, and the six previews together stay well under the ~723 KB the set weighs today.
- [ ] The new screenshot shows the T-Play product page, not the Telecentro home.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green; Lighthouse still ≥ 0.90.

input.title: 26 · Aurora: the bottom of the page turns olive-green as you scroll
input.description:
## The defect

Scrolling down, a large soft stain grows behind the content and dominates the contact section and footer. It reads as a stray shadow that came unstuck from the footer. It is not a shadow — it is the aurora.

`src/lib/motion/math.ts`:

```ts
export function auroraStyle(p: number) {
  return {
    filter: `hue-rotate(${Math.round(p * 260)}deg) saturate(${round(1 + 0.4 * p, 3)})`,
    opacity: 0.45 + 0.55 * Math.min(1, p * 2.5),
    translateY: `${round(-12 * p)}vh`,
  }
}
```

Measured at the bottom of the document: `opacity: 1`, `filter: hue-rotate(260deg) saturate(1.4)`, `translateY(-12vh)`.

Two things compound. The opacity ramp reaches **1.0 at only 40% of the document**, so the blobs run at full strength for the entire second half. And `hue-rotate(260deg)` takes the cyan accent (~187°) round to ~87° — yellow-green. Full-strength olive over the last three sections. Confirmed on a screenshot at the footer: the whole upper-right quadrant is a green smear, and the contact card sits on top of it.

## Not a regression — a spec that does not survive contact

`MOTION_SPEC` §4 does specify `hue-rotate(p·260deg)` and `opacity .45 → 1` in the first 40%. This is faithfully implemented; it just looks wrong on the real page, where the mock's short scroll never reached high `p` with this much page below it.

So this is a **design tuning decision, not a bug fix**, and it needs a call rather than a "correct" answer. The options, roughly:

1. Cap the hue sweep so it stays inside the cyan → violet family the palette owns (the design's secondary is violet at ~260°, not green) — e.g. rotate toward violet and stop, instead of a full 260° sweep past green.
2. Flatten the opacity ramp, or ramp it back down over the last stretch so the footer is calm.
3. Both.

Whichever is chosen, the aurora must stay decorative and must not cost contrast: the contact card and the footer sit over it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `auroraStyle` is unit-tested at `p = 0, .2, .4, .7, 1` against the chosen curve — the math lives in `math.ts` and stays testable without a DOM.
- [ ] No hue in the sweep leaves the cyan-violet family (assert the resolved hue range, do not eyeball it).
- [ ] The contact card's text and the footer still meet 4.5:1 with the aurora at its strongest, in both themes.
- [ ] `MOTION_SPEC` §4 is the read-only source of truth, so the deviation is recorded in `docs/superpowers/specs/` with the reason, not silently applied.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green; Lighthouse accessibility does not drop.

## What is left after that

Nueve issues creados en Linear. Todo medido contra el mock renderizado (`handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html`) a 1512×950, no a ojo.

**El hallazgo que cambia el plan:** cuatro de tus quejas son el mismo bug.

`container-page` usa `max-width: 1200px` con `box-sizing: border-box` (el reset de Tailwind), así que el padding de 48px va **adentro** del tope. El mock usa `content-box`. Resultado: todo el sitio es 96px más angosto y arranca 48px más adentro que el diseño.

| | Mock | Nuestro | Con `content-box` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Columna de contenido | 1200 | 1104 | **1200** |
| Columna del hero | 564 | 516 | **564** |
| H1 | 296px (4 líneas) | 380px (5 líneas) | **304px (4 líneas)** |
| Consola | ~562 | 509 | **564** |

Lo verifiqué inyectando una sola línea de CSS. El título estirado y la terminal chica se arreglan solos.

**El otro root cause:** `.stack` es un grid cuya columna implícita se dimensiona al `max-content` de la marquesina. `document.scrollWidth` da **3588px** contra un viewport de 1512 (el mock: 1512). De ahí salen tres síntomas: el scroll horizontal, el subtítulo a x=1912 (fuera de pantalla), y el blur derecho que nunca ves — la máscara es simétrica (8%/92%), pero el 92% de 3384px está fuera de la pantalla. `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` lo lleva de 3588 a 1512.

**Los issues**

| | Bloquea | |
|---|---|---|
| [PV3-24](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-24) | **19** · Container `content-box` | Urgent — bloquea 20 y 27 |
| [PV3-27](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-27) | **22** · Stack: overflow + 4-5 filas | Urgent |
| [PV3-25](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-25) | **20** · Nav alineado al container | ← 19 |
| [PV3-26](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-26) | **21** · Toggle de idioma en dos líneas | |
| [PV3-28](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-28) | **23** · Timeline dot + "también con" | |
| [PV3-29](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-29) | **24** · Shimmer se corta | |
| [PV3-30](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-30) | **25** · Telecentro `/t-play` | |
| [PV3-31](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-31) | **26** · Aurora verde oliva | |
| [PV3-32](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-32) | **27** · Fidelidad del hero | ← 19 |

**Causas exactas de los demás:**

- **Toggle de idioma**: `.toggle` es `display: grid` y el texto suelto ` / en` se convierte en un *anonymous grid item* → segunda fila. `nowrap` no puede ayudar, no están en la misma línea. Medido: `scrollHeight` 36 vs `clientHeight` 34.
- **Dot del timeline**: `margin-top: 28px` a dedo. Centro del dot a 34px del tope de la card, centro del logo a 49px. 15px de error en las cinco.
- **"También con" vertical**: `.also-list` no tiene *ninguna* regla CSS, cae a `display: block`.
- **Shimmer**: `left: -40%` + `translateX(250%)` termina con el borde derecho de la banda justo sobre el borde del frame — y `ease-in-out` desacelera exactamente ahí. El handoff dice `left: 0` y `-100% → 250%`, que la deja fuera de pantalla al saltar.
- **La "sombra que crece" no es una sombra**: es la aurora. `hue-rotate(p·260deg)` lleva el cian (~187°) a ~87° = verde oliva, y el opacity llega a 1.0 al 40% del documento. Se ve en el screenshot del footer.

**Dos cosas necesitan tu decisión, están anotadas en los issues:**

1. El handoff especifica **3 filas** en el stack (`DESIGN_SPEC` §7). Vos pedís 4-5. Lo escribí como desvío deliberado del handoff.
2. Lo mismo con la aurora: `MOTION_SPEC` §4 especifica ese `hue-rotate` de 260°. Está implementado fiel — se ve mal igual. El issue plantea las opciones (cortar el barrido en violeta, aplanar el opacity, o ambas) en vez de elegir por vos.

Y una pregunta suelta: el **link** de la card de Telecentro, ¿va también a `/t-play` o queda en la raíz? Por defecto dejé solo el screenshot, que es lo que pediste.

# 17 · Playwright smoke + Lighthouse CI — spec

Issue: [PV3-22](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-22) · Branch: `feat/17-e2e-lighthouse`
Design: design doc §6, §9 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §13

## Goal

The end-to-end safety net, plus the performance budget. Small on purpose: 304 unit tests
already cover every formula, so this block only has to prove the DOM plumbing runs in a
real browser.

## Context

`bun test` covers content, i18n, all the motion math, contrast and the a11y invariants.
None of it opens a browser. Every block so far verified its own DOM work by running
shipped scripts against hand-written stubs — which is honest, but not the same as a
browser.

Two things are still unverified for exactly that reason:

- Whether the focus ring is **visually unclipped**. `overflow: hidden` on `.row`,
  `.preview` and `.edge` could crop a 2px offset ring on an element sitting flush
  against them. Issue 16 flagged this and could not close it.
- Whether the frame budget holds on a throttled machine rather than an M4.

CI today runs lint, test and build on Bun 1.4.0.

## Scope

### 1. Playwright

`bun add -d @playwright/test`. This is the one dependency this block adds, and it is
justified: nothing else drives a real browser.

`playwright.config.ts`: Chromium only, `webServer` running `bun run preview` against the
static build, `baseURL` from it, retries 0 locally and 1 in CI, trace on first retry.

### 2. The six smoke tests — `e2e/smoke.spec.ts`

Each asserts something a unit test structurally cannot:

1. **The hero boots.** After the boot sequence, the `h1` and all five `[data-boot]`
   elements are at opacity 1. Guards the whole `boot.ts` timeline in a real event loop.
2. **The theme toggle round-trips.** Click, assert `documentElement.dataset.theme` and
   `style.colorScheme` both flipped, reload, assert it persisted.
3. **The language toggle navigates.** Click, land on `/en`, assert `<html lang="en">` and
   that the `h1` matches `content.en.h1a`.
4. **A reveal fires on scroll.** A card below the fold starts at opacity 0 and reaches 1
   after scrolling to it.
5. **The method sticky advances.** Scroll through the 280vh track and assert the active
   step index goes 0 → 4 and the indicator text tracks it.
6. **`reduce` mounts no canvas.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated:
   `page.locator('canvas')` has count 0, and the hero text is visible from the first
   frame.

Plus the one issue 16 could not do:

7. **The focus ring is not clipped.** Tab to each interactive element and assert its
   `getBoundingClientRect`, expanded by the 2px ring and its 2px offset, is inside the
   client rect of every `overflow: hidden` ancestor. If an element fails, fix the CSS —
   do not delete the assertion.

Keep it at these seven. A large E2E suite is slow and flaky, and this one exists to catch
what unit tests cannot reach, not to re-cover them.

### 3. Lighthouse CI

`bun add -d @lhci/cli`. Mobile preset against the static build.

Thresholds, all **error** level: Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices and SEO each
≥ 90.

If Performance misses, degrade in the order `MOTION_SPEC` §13 fixes — shimmer, then
aurora, then node count — and **write down in the PR what was degraded and the before/after
numbers**. Do not lower the threshold, and do not degrade preemptively: measure first.

### 4. CI wiring

Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the existing `check` job stays as is, and a second job
runs the build once, then Playwright and Lighthouse against it. Cache the Playwright
browser download.

Total CI time must stay under 5 minutes. Report the actual number.

### 5. Scripts

Add `test:e2e` (`playwright test`) and `test:lh` (`lhci autorun`). `tests/scaffold.test.ts`
asserts the exact set of package scripts, so it needs updating — that is expected, not a
reason to avoid adding them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The seven Playwright tests pass locally three runs in a row with no flake.
- [ ] They pass in CI.
- [ ] Lighthouse reports ≥ 90 on all four categories, mobile, against the built site.
- [ ] The focus-ring test genuinely fails when a ring is clipped — prove it by temporarily narrowing an ancestor, then revert.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` still pass; the scaffold script test is updated.
- [ ] Total CI wall time under 5 minutes.

## Out of scope

Visual regression snapshots. Cross-browser runs — Chromium only; the design targets
evergreen browsers and a second engine doubles CI time for little here. Deploy (issue 18).
